findings.title: brace-expansion exponential-time processing in Office lint tooling

normalized_input.claimed_control: no input bound or timeout inside the affected package
preconditions: A caller must pass an attacker-controlled brace pattern to the nested minimatch instance.
normalized_input.impact: denial of service in the calling Node process

affected_locations.label: vulnerable locked instance
affected_locations.detail: The exact brace-expansion 2.1.1 and minimatch 9.0.9 instances are marked development-only.

affected_locations.label: development entrypoint
affected_locations.detail: office-addin-lint is development-only and introduces the typescript-eslint chain.

boundary_assessment.policy_basis: Root SECURITY.md plus development-only lock metadata and the supported Office lint configuration

evidence: The vulnerable package instance is marked dev:true.
The exact caller uses minimatch only for allowDefaultProject patterns in the optional project-service path.
The supported lint configuration enables neither projectService nor allowDefaultProject.
No product or production dependency path includes this instance.
counterevidence: The upstream package defect is genuine but dependency presence alone does not establish an EMR4 security boundary.
A trusted developer could deliberately change lint configuration to enable the optional sink.
findings.recommended_next_step: Register the alert open with owner/SLA, leave native disposition unchanged pending explicit authority, and reassess when the supported dependency graph or lint configuration changes.
